decision.title: Calendars and languages in the formatting functions (packet )

body.p: , after , , , , , , , . Replaces 's "calendars other than AD and ISO and languages other than English" and their places: the fallback markers of src/function_library_format_date.c and the English-only words of src/format.c.

item.p: One CLDR mechanism (glossary , , ; src/cldr.c, src/cldr_internal.h): the language tag reader, the locale truncation (de_AT, de, root), the urn:sxml: + CLDR path URIs and the LDML tree builder moved out of src/collation_tailoring.c, as asked once a second user exists. A file is read into a table of its leaf elements by distinguished path (every attribute but draft and references, in document order; only the paths below the caller's prefixes are kept) with its aliases; lookups go along the locale chain, skip CLDR's inheritance marker "↑↑↑" and follow aliases (UTS #35, Part 1, 4.1.3: the longest prefix with an alias, relative "../" steps, at most 16). The collation tailorings read collations/defaultCollation and collations/collation[@type=T] /cr through it, with 's behaviour unchanged.

The feature sxml_localization_feature() ("localization", additive in processor.h, in sxml_all_optional_features), and the additive resource kind SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_LOCALE_DATA: urn:sxml:locale-data: + main/<locale>.xml, rbnf/<locale>.xml, supplemental/supplementalData.xml or supplemental/ordinals.xml, the CLDR files as CLDR publishes them (no generated tables: the task file's src/language_tables.c and its generator gave way to 's data from the host). A language table (glossary ) is built at a tag's first use and kept in the processor with negative answers, for up to 64 tags (src/language_table.c).

Names (UTS #35, Part 4, section 2): the wide names of the format context for months, days, eras (eraAbbr, as "AD") and day periods (the abbreviated "AM"), with the abbreviated names of the format and stand-alone contexts as abbreviations; a width modifier takes the longest abbreviation that fits, else cuts the name, counting code points. Upper and lower case use Unicode's full mappings ("MÄRZ", "DREISSIG"); without a presentation modifier a CLDR name keeps its own case ("n. Chr."), and title case keeps the case of letters after the first. A language has names when a file of its chain other than root is served; without them "[Language: en]" and English, as before.

Calendars (F&O 4.0, 9.9.4.8; src/calendar.c): BE (CLDR's buddhist), JE (japanese: the eras of supplementalData's calendarData by their Gregorian start dates, after the inherited Gregorian eras), OS (the Julian calendar from the day number, E. G. Richards' algorithm) and AH (the tabular islamic-civil calendar: 30-year cycle, leap years 2, 5, 7, 10, 13, 16, 18, 21, 24, 26, 29, epoch 16 July 622 Julian). Day of year, week of year and week of month are those of the calendar's own years and months, a week belonging to its Thursday. The other designators, a calendar in a namespace, a calendar without names (no feature, no data, BE and JE without supplementalData), and years beyond ±10^12 in a converted calendar keep "[Calendar: AD]". English with AD and ISO needs no data, as before.

Words (src/spell_out.c; glossary , ): CLDR's rule-based number formatting (UTS #35, Part 3, section 6, with ICU's rule syntax): rule sets of the SpelloutRules and OrdinalRules groupings of the most specific rbnf file of the chain other than root; divisors by radix, bracketed text as two rules and ICU's rollback, →→ ←← =…= with a rule set or a decimal pattern, and $(ordinal,…)$ by the ordinal plural rules of ordinals.xml (integer operands; $(cardinal,…)$ takes "other"). Run with an explicit stack of 64 frames and 4,096 steps (); integers below 2^64, larger ones in English. The text in parentheses of the format modifier (F&O 4.0, 4.8.1) or xsl:number's ordinal (XSLT 4.0, 12.4) chooses the rule set: %name a public set (a missing one the language's default of the kind its name says), -ending the first set of the family whose words end so ("-er" gives German "zehnter", "-a" Italian "quinta"), else spellout-ordinal (then -masculine) for ordinals and spellout-cardinal (then spellout-numbering) for cardinals. Ordinals of digits take only the suffix of digits-ordinal ("1er", "3.º"); German's rules have none, so no suffix. W is upper case, Ww each word's first letter, w the rules' own text. English keeps sxml's own words () unless a rule set is named (%spellout-ordinal-verbose). Through sxml_number_words in sxml_integer_formatting, so format-integer, xsl:number and the date pictures ([Dwo]) share it.

Languages asked for: $language of the date functions and of fn:format-integer, xsl:number's lang; the empty sequence or "" is the dynamic context's default language (sxml_dynamic_context_ configuration.default_language, "en" when empty).

Vendored (, ): third_party/cldr/common gains main/ (root, en, de, de_AT, es, fr, it, nl), rbnf/ (en, de, es, fr, it, nl) and supplemental/supplementalData.xml and ordinals.xml, CLDR 47, hashes in the README (4.1 MB). The QT4 driver serves them (and the XSLT driver through it) and sets the default language a test asks for (default-language fr-CA). The sxml command embeds them (apps/sxml/embed-cldr-data.cmake, which replaces embed-collation- data): main/ reduced to the months, days, dayPeriods and eras of the gregorian, buddhist, japanese and islamic calendars, supplementalData to calendarData, with CLDR's paths and values. JavaScript hosts answer the kind 'locale-data'.

Measured (release drivers, against 4d78eba): QT4 fn-format-date XQ40 125 to 137 of 138, XP40 124 to 136 (the 12 de cases); fn-format-integer 87 to 94 (032, 032-fr, 032-it, 065, 066, 076, 077); fn-default-language 5 to 6 (006, fr-CA); app-spec-examples XQ40 1,484 to 1,486, XP40 1,351 to 1,353; fn-format-dateTime, fn-format-time, fn-format-number, misc-BuiltInKeywords, fn-function-lookup unchanged. XT40 number 265 to 274 of 274 (languages_for_numbering de, it, fr, ICU_spellout, ordinal_scheme_name); format-date, format-date-en, format-number, avt, date, sort unchanged. The gate's 38 named cases: QT4 20 of 20, XT40 9 of 9, every named case run passes; no format-date or format-integer case lost. The 8 cases of fn-format- integer still not run are numbering sequences (Arabic-Indic digits, circled digits, Greek, CJK), not languages.

Sizes (wasm preset, stripped / gzip -9, before and after at 4d78eba): sxml.wasm 2,342,948 / 820,110 to 2,347,868 / 821,993 (+4,920: the calendar conversions, the number-words hook, Unicode case in names; the core was over its 2,200,000 / 770,000 budget before this packet); sxml-full.wasm 6,949,025 / 1,572,066 to 6,981,128 / 1,585,595 (+32,103); the CLI module 8,207,589 / 1,825,633 to 8,573,783 / 1,866,011 (+366,194, nearly all the embedded CLDR names). Within 's full and CLI budgets (7,000,000 / 2,450,000; 9,000,000 / 2,000,000); no budget raised.

Left: other calendars (the fallback F&O allows); CLDR's parentLocales (es_419 and the like are found by truncation only); the cardinal plural rules; date formats of CLDR (sxml formats pictures, not patterns); a language's digits other than ASCII in names.
